title: C-Suite 1:1 prep & follow-ups — scratchpad
content:
Context: quick prep notes for weekly 1:1 with CTO (Samir) and subsequent exec staff sync. This is a personal scratchpad — messy, highlight Qs, data to surface, asks and a short post-meeting follow-up plan.

Attendees: Samir (CTO) — primary; me (Asha) — agenda lead. Optional drop-ins: Laura (product ops), Keon (infra).

High-level goals for the 1:1:
- Align on Dedicated capacity rollout timeline + critical path items for March/April pilot.
- Confirm SLA phrasing for enterprise pilot contracts (what we can promise now vs. later).
- Get thumbs-up on experimental routing policy for cost-first mode (need green light to wire telemetry).
- Surface the recent regression in streaming latency on MPT-7B family and propose mitigation (fallback model / reduced batch window).

Stuff to bring (data):
- 7-day latency p50/p95 for hosted API by model family (bring quick table).
- Cost per generated token delta for quantized vs. baseline for the most common sequence length (avg 128).
- Dedicated capacity beta usage vs. forecast (three customers, booked GPU hours).
- One pager on private deployment pilot (legal redlines summarized).

Priority talking points (short bullets):
1) Dedicated rollout: current blocker = infra autoscaling bug (SRE already has PR but needs signoff). Ask: allocate one infra sprint slice to complete autoscaler tests and canary logic.
2) SLA language: product/legal want 99.5% availability; ops warns that's optimistic for first 3 months. Ask: propose phased SLA (preview: 99.0 -> GA: 99.5) and rollback plan.
3) Streaming latency regression: provide example trace + top 3 suspected causes (kv cache miss pattern, batching window change, kernel selection bug). Ask: authorize canary fallback to earlier runtime for MPT models for 72 hours.
4) Routing policy experiment: detail risk (cost vs. quality), telemetry needs, and expected user-visible change. Ask: approve telemetry tag and 1% traffic experiment.

Open questions for Samir (notes-to-self phrasing):
- Can we fast-track a contract amendment to delay strict SLA for pilot customers? (legal implications?)
- Do we want to make the routing experiment opt-in per-customer or global 1%? Pros/cons shorthand.
- Resource ask: if we reassign one eng pair to autoscaler, which team loses capacity? (impacts releases)

Decision boxes to put in meeting:
- Approve 72-hr runtime fallback for MPT streaming regression? (yes/no)
- Approve 1% routing experiment for cost-first mode? (yes/no)
- Approve phased SLA wording for pilot customers? (yes/no)

Parking lot (non-blocking, keep short):
- Longer-term: invest in prefix cache profiler to reduce cold-start token cost.
- Consider product-level flags for per-route quantization suggestions (post-launch).

Draft script / opening lines: "Samir — quick status: Dedicated pilot is primed but blocked on autoscaler tests; I have three asks that will unblock or de-risk the next 6 weeks: slot a small infra sprint for autoscaler, approve a short runtime fallback for MPT streaming regression, and green-light a 1% telemetry-backed routing experiment. I can run through the numbers in 6 minutes."

Follow-up plan (post-1:1) — action items (short, assigned, due):
- A1: Draft phased SLA amendment language and send to legal for review. Owner: Asha. Due: 2026-03-17.
- A2: Create 1-page autoscaler risk log + link to PR #789; ping SRE for test ETA. Owner: Keon (infra). CC: Samir. Due: 2026-03-13.
- A3: Prepare telemetry spec for routing experiment (metrics, flags, rollbacks). Owner: Laura (product ops). Due: 2026-03-15.
- A4: Run canary fallback for MPT models for 72 hours and capture latency + error delta. Owner: Runtime team (Samir to OK). Due: start by 2026-03-12, end by 2026-03-15.
- A5: Customer comms: draft email to pilot customers describing phased SLA and expected timeline. Owner: CS (Jared). Due: 2026-03-18.

Notes-to-self & scratch fragments (useful one-liners to remember in meeting):
- If Samir hesitates on routing experiment, propose a telemetry-only dry-run first (no routing change).
- Keep legal's language non-binding for pilot customers ("target" vs. "guarantee").
- Cite the recent P95 spike on 2026-03-04 as the reason for quick fallback — have raw trace ready.

After meeting checklist (very brief):
- Update this doc with decisions (tick boxes).
- Create JIRA tasks for each approved action (link in linked_artifacts).
- Send recap email to exec staff and copy owners.

Quick mental model to carry into conversation: we want to move fast but avoid promise creep on enterprise SLAs until Dedicated has two full-scale pilots running without major incidents. Use fallbacks + limited experiments to buy time.

End of scratchpad — will convert into tidy follow-up email if decisions are made.
